source_references.publisher: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)
source_references.title: Resourcing Higher Education — Human resources in higher education
source_references.locator: OECD describes a continuum from academic roles to professional/administrative roles supporting teaching, research and engagement; it notes role mixes differ by institution and system.
source_references.supports: Academic teaching/research and professional services are distinguishable role contexts; education institutions and national systems vary.

source_references.publisher: United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO)
source_references.title: Recommendation concerning the Status of Higher-Education Teaching Personnel
source_references.locator: UNESCO calls the 1997 Recommendation the only global standard-setting instrument dedicated specifically to higher-education teaching personnel and describes its scope as people engaged to teach, undertake scholarship or research, or provide educational services to students or the community.
source_references.supports: Teaching, scholarship/research and educational service are distinct but related higher-education functions; this parent is not ordinary school-level teaching by definition.
source_references.claim_limit: A fixed four-area taxonomy, exact role placements, or national qualification equivalence.

subgroups.description: Use quantitative and computational approaches to study social questions, population patterns, and relationships. source_references.title: TC 65 — Industrial-process measurement, control and automation: committee structure
source_references.locator: Committee structure lists system aspects, measurement/control devices, industrial networks, devices/integration in enterprise systems, OT cybersecurity, digital factory, life-cycle management, safety/security and reliability work groups.
source_references.supports: Measurement/control devices, networks, system aspects and integration are recognized international technical scopes within industrial-process automation.
source_references.claim_limit: A universal job taxonomy, an exact Sifter subgroup count, or that every manufacturing/assembly role is automation work.

source_references.publisher: International Society of Automation (ISA); ANSI/ISA and IEC 62264 standards family
source_references.title: ISA-95 Series of Standards: Enterprise-Control System Integration
source_references.locator: ISA's official overview describes levels from physical process, sensing/actuation, PLC/DCS/SCADA control, manufacturing operations management/MES, to enterprise planning/logistics; it emphasizes activities and interfaces rather than a technology-specific taxonomy.
source_references.supports: Distinct automation and manufacturing-system functions exist across process control and operations integration; the model clarifies boundaries and dependencies.
source_references.claim_limit: A prescribed learning order, an exact specialization count, or a credential requirement for every practitioner.

source_references.title: Pathway guide — Commercial Real Estate (January 2026)
source_references.locator: Pathway competencies include landlord/tenant, property management, property records, rental appraisal, leasing/letting, purchase/sale, valuation, development appraisals and strategic real-estate consultancy.
source_references.supports: Property transactions/leasing, management, valuation and development work are distinct competency areas in a professional pathway.
source_references.claim_limit: That every listed competency is a separate Sifter subgroup or that one pathway defines all countries' occupational regulations.

source_references.title: How to attain the Purchase and Sale competency
source_references.locator: Defines purchase/sale competency around acquisition and disposal of freehold/leasehold property, investment property, due diligence and property-market constraints; competency appears in several pathways.
source_references.supports: Property transaction work is specific to real-property interests and can appear across related pathways.
source_references.claim_limit: Jurisdiction-specific legal authorization or a separate subgroup requirement by itself.

areas_of_specialization.label: Real Estate Valuation and Appraisal

areas_of_specialization.boundary: Business interests and intangible assets are separate asset classes under IVS; valuation skill alone does not make a role real-estate work. Development valuation and development appraisal are related but distinct outputs.

source_references.title: International Valuation Standards — asset standards
source_references.locator: IVSC identifies separate asset standards for businesses/business interests, intangible assets, plant/equipment/infrastructure, real-property interests and development property.
source_references.supports: Real-property valuation is a distinct asset-specific practice; general valuation of businesses or intangibles is not automatically real-estate valuation.
source_references.claim_limit: A role taxonomy, a certification, or the claim that all business valuers belong in D051.

source_references.publisher: ISO/TC 258 Project, Programme and Portfolio Management
source_references.title: ISO 21502:2020 — Guidance on project management
source_references.locator: Page states that ISO 21502 provides project-management guidelines for any organization, sector, project type or delivery approach, including predictive, iterative, adaptive, hybrid and agile approaches; it expressly does not provide programme or portfolio management guidance.
source_references.supports: Project delivery/lifecycle practice is distinct from programme and portfolio management; delivery approach is a method dimension rather than automatically a separate specialization.
source_references.claim_limit: A fixed project-management subgroup list, specific role mappings, or a claim that every agile tool/credential is universally required.

source_references.publisher: ISO/TC 258 Project, Programme and Portfolio Management
source_references.title: ISO 21503:2022 — Guidance on programme management
source_references.locator: The published scope says the guidance applies to programme management across organization types, sizes and sectors, and describes terms, concepts, prerequisites, practices, roles and responsibilities.
source_references.supports: Programme management is a distinct practice area from project management; evidence-backed programme learning should not be collapsed into project delivery.
source_references.claim_limit: A universal subgroup count or role placement in the repository.

source_references.publisher: ISO/TC 258 Project, Programme and Portfolio Management
source_references.title: ISO/TC 258 published project, programme and portfolio standards; ISO 21504:2022 guidance on portfolio management
source_references.locator: The published deliverables list separately identifies ISO 21502 project management, ISO 21503 programme management, ISO 21504 portfolio management, and ISO 21505 governance guidance.
source_references.supports: The standards family treats these as related but separately scoped practice areas; portfolio management should not be inserted into D032 without resolving its title/scope.
source_references.claim_limit: A decision that D032 must be renamed or that portfolio roles belong in another particular domain.

source_references.publisher: APQC; retail framework developed with Microsoft subject-matter expertise
source_references.title: APQC Process Classification Framework (PCF) - Retail - PDF Version 6.1.1
source_references.locator: Retail capability map, PDF pp. 15-18: distinct capability headings include Store Operations, Merchandising, Customer Relationship Management, Develop and Manage Customer Experience, Develop and Manage Omni Channels, and Market Products and Services; associated activities include checkout, floor merchandising/promotions, inventory, customer service, channel strategy and customer satisfaction.
source_references.supports: A global retail process framework recognizes separable retail process/capability areas that support a concise student-facing split among customer-facing sales/service, merchandising/product planning, and retail store/channel operations.
source_references.claim_limit: This is an enterprise process/capability map, not an academic specialization standard, occupational classification or mandated subgroup count. The proposed three-area set is an internal learner-facing synthesis. E-commerce/omnichannel is retained as a channel context within operations and customer experience, not treated as a standalone area solely because the framework names channels. Geographic scope: international/global industry framework.

source_references.title: Retail Sales; WorldSkills Occupational Standards

source_references.supports: Independent international vocational evidence corroborates the integrated customer-facing, product-display and operational task clusters used to define D085 specialization boundaries.
source_references.claim_limit: The public profile is an occupation/skill benchmark, not a taxonomy of academic specializations or evidence that each repository role belongs in D085. source_references.title: GLI Standards
source_references.locator: Published standards catalogue: GLI-11 Gaming Devices; GLI-14 finite scratch-ticket and pull-tab systems; GLI-15 electronic Bingo and Keno; GLI-19 Interactive Gaming Systems; GLI-24/25 electronic table games; GLI-31 electronic raffle systems; GLI-33 event-wagering systems. The page states jurisdictions retain authority to set their own standards and many use GLI standards as a starting point.
source_references.supports: Independent technical standards evidence that casino devices/table games, bingo/keno, lottery-style games, interactive systems and event wagering are distinct product/system contexts in the global gaming ecosystem.
source_references.claim_limit: GLI is a testing/standards provider, not a regulator or academic accreditor; jurisdictions decide which standards apply. The catalogue supports product/system boundaries, not a universal occupational taxonomy or proof that repository roles belong in D086. Geographic scope: standards used across jurisdictions, with legal adoption jurisdiction-specific.

source_references.publisher: World Lottery Association (WLA), Security and Risk Management Committee
source_references.title: WLA Security Control Standard (WLA-SCS):2024
source_references.locator: Scope and contents, pp. 2-3; Annex B sections L.6-L.10 (sports/esports/horse-race betting, interactive video lottery terminals, random-number generation, online games, game design/approval); Annex C S controls for development of gaming systems and provision of gaming services.
source_references.supports: An international gaming-sector standard explicitly distinguishes betting, lottery/video-lottery, online games, game design/approval and gaming-system/service development as different operational and product/system work contexts.
source_references.claim_limit: The standard concerns security, integrity and controls, not an academic specialization taxonomy or occupation-to-domain fit. Its multijurisdictional games annex is specifically US MUSL-related; do not generalize that annex's jurisdictional requirements. Geographic scope: international gaming-sector standard, with explicitly jurisdiction-specific annex provisions.

source_references.title: National Core Professional Dog Grooming Educational Standards
source_references.locator: Framework states six educational domains: groomer safety; pet safety/humane treatment; sanitation; dog anatomy/physical characteristics; professional grooming practice; professionalism/business. Core practices include grooming methods by coat type, bathing/drying, safe handling, humane behavior management and client communication.
source_references.supports: Dog grooming is a defined technical practice area distinct from general pet care and training, with species/coat knowledge, sanitation, safe handling and grooming techniques.
source_references.claim_limit: AKC is a U.S. national organization and the standards are dog-specific, not a global taxonomy for all animal grooming or proof of any role's D090 fit. Geographic scope: United States.

source_references.title: Standards of Excellence for Animal Sanctuaries
source_references.locator: Standards overview separates facility operations standards from animal-specific care standards; describes 26 care/operations standards developed with sanctuary professionals, animal advocates and veterinarians and reviewed through a formal revision process.
source_references.supports: Rescue, rehabilitation and sanctuary animal care form a distinct service context with animal-specific welfare and facility-operation requirements, separable from private pet grooming/boarding.
source_references.claim_limit: GFAS standards are voluntary and apply to sanctuary/rescue contexts; they are not a universal animal-care occupation taxonomy and do not establish role fit or a required subgroup count. Geographic scope: facilities worldwide.

source_references.publisher: Australian Government Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, training.gov.au
source_references.title: TLI41225 Certificate IV in Motor Vehicle Driver Training
source_references.locator: Qualification details list distinct units including TLIM0008 Conduct car driver training and TLIM0013 Conduct motorcycle rider training, alongside heavy-vehicle driving trainer units.
source_references.supports: An independent national vocational framework distinguishes car, motorcycle and heavy-vehicle training competencies, corroborating that these are not interchangeable instructor contexts.
source_references.claim_limit: Australian qualification structure, not a global taxonomy or universally required credential. It supports the existence of distinct training contexts, not exact labels/count or role-domain fit. Geographic scope: Australia.

source_references.publisher: Driver and Vehicle Standards Agency, UK Department for Transport
source_references.title: National standard for driver and rider training
source_references.locator: Introduction and role scope: training for cars/light vans (category B) and mopeds/motorcycles (category A), licence-acquisition and post-test programmes; distinct in-car/on-bike practical delivery and classroom instruction expectations.
source_references.supports: Driver/rider instruction has distinct car/light-van and motorcycle/moped contexts with vehicle-specific instructor competence and delivery requirements.
source_references.claim_limit: UK national standard, not a global instructor taxonomy or a universal legal requirement. It does not define the repository's exact area count or validate individual role links. Geographic scope: England, Scotland and Wales.

source_references.publisher: United Nations Economic Commission for Europe
source_references.title: Convention on Road Traffic (1968), consolidated text
source_references.locator: Annex 6, paragraph 5: permit categories A (motorcycles), B (vehicles up to 3,500 kg and up to eight passenger seats), C (goods vehicles above 3,500 kg) and D (passenger vehicles with more than eight seats).
source_references.supports: International road-permit categories distinguish motorcycle, light-vehicle, heavy-goods and large-passenger vehicle operation; these provide a defensible vehicle-scope axis for instruction areas.
source_references.claim_limit: The Convention defines driving-permit categories, not instructor specializations or a student-facing subgroup count. Domestic law implements and may adapt categories. Geographic scope: international treaty adopted by contracting parties.

source_references.locator: Committee scope and working groups covering geometrical product specifications, tolerancing, measurement equipment, calibration, measurement uncertainty and coordinate measuring machines.

source_references.title: WorldSkills Occupational Standards: CNC Milling (2024)
source_references.locator: Occupation description and standards: CNC machine setup/programming, precision manufacture from technical drawings, machining of metals and other solids, and dimensional checking.
source_references.supports: Precision CNC machining is a distinct manufacturing practice involving programmed tool motion, accurate part production, drawing interpretation and inspection; it supports a toolmaking/precision-machining area.
source_references.claim_limit: WorldSkills competition benchmark, not a complete taxonomy or universal credential requirement. Toolmaking and CNC machining overlap but are not synonyms. Geographic scope: international reference.

source_references.title: WorldSkills Occupational Standards: CNC Turning (2024)

source_references.claim_limit: International competition standard; it establishes an occupational practice and task scope, not a universal study-path count. Geographic scope: international reference.
